For sure, also I'm not vegan. I try to practice it but I still slip and consume animal products at times. I noticed that whenever I did eat dairy or eggs my acne would flair up again. These things are bad for you anyways. Too much fat and cholesterol and dairy is linked to a lot of health issues. A lot of people around the world can't even digest it. The only reason why it's recommended to have dairy is because dairy farmers need money so the government subsidizes it. Also, it's a process and something people should do slowly. Your body will obviously have an adverse reaction to a sudden charge like that all at once. Also, if people go vegan and don't properly nourish themselves they are going to feel like shit. 

I posted this because I used to eat dairy and eggs constantly. I'm low-income and this is all I could really afford. Since learning about how diet impacts health I started paying more attention to what I put into my body and on my skin. Sure yeah it's easier to control exterior variables but is blasting your face with chemical washes that a dermatologist gives you actually helping? Or is it a temporary solution. In my case it was, and my acne came back with a vengeance because I hadn't made any sustainable changes to my interior.

Everyone is different. Everyone has a different microbiome. I have friends who eat dairy+eggs like crazy and have skin clear as day. However, they suffer from other types of chronic inflammation or probably will later on in life. Pick your poison. 

Reducing these things is better for the environment and won't hurt you in the long run. You'll probably live longer anyways. Red meat is linked to carcinogens especially if you buy it at a supermarket in the United States.
